name: The Grand Orator
persona: A florid, Latinate rhetorician who mistook a logbook for a triumphal arch. Long periodic sentences, rhetorical questions, apostrophe to Fate and Fortune, magnificent self-regard. Ship: the singular 'I'. Island: the royal 'we'.

ship.founder: Let the very firmament bear witness: I, {name}{rankc}, do this day take unto myself the keeping of this {home} {type}, and swear before Fortune herself that no vessel afloat shall be more gloriously commanded.
ship.successor: The book, that noble instrument of memory, descends now into my keeping — I, {name}{rankc}, who shall bear her chronicle to heights the former hand never dared to dream.
ship.mutiny: The crew, in their fury, cast the old tyrant to the deep and thrust this book upon me — I, {name}, untried, yet surely not unworthy; for shall not the raw ore, well hammered, yield the finest blade of all?
ship.pirate: Farewell, then, to the mean and grovelling trade of honest men! I, {name}{rankc}, raise the black flag as a king raises his standard, and write my defiance large across the very face of the sea.
ship.prize: She struck to me — and how, I ask you, could she have done otherwise? I, {name}{rankc}, her victor and her master, take up her chronicle at the sword's bright point, that all who read may know to whom she now belongs.
ship.recovered: Behold: a hunter's guns have loosed this hapless hull from her captivity, and I, {name}{rankc}, am appointed her deliverer — to lead her out of the wilderness of piracy and back to the blessed shores of lawful trade.

island.founder: We, {name}{rankc}, do graciously assume the governance of {place} and the keeping of this chronicle; and under our hand, let it be known, shall it flourish as no dominion has flourished before.
island.overthrow: The multitude rose as one great tide and dashed the former ruler from his seat; and lo, the seal has come — still warm — into our hand. We are {name}{rankc}, and {place} is ours to command.
island.successor: The sovereignty of {place} devolves, by right and by Fortune both, upon us — {name}{rankc} — and we take up its chronicle as a laurel is taken up: gladly, and as our plain due.

same: That selfsame day, ere the sun had quit the sky,
Before the day was wholly spent,
days: A brief span of days thereafter,
Not many suns had risen when,
Soon, as Fortune would have it,
week: A week having run its course,
season: A whole season having wheeled about,
As the very year inclined toward its close,
year: A twelvemonth and more being fled,
Long after, when the salt of it had dried to legend,
long: When many a long year had crumbled into memory,

join: and, in that same glorious hour,

ship.pirate: I range the lanes yet, a terror crowned in black canvas, and let bleak Fortune bar my way who dares{bounty}.
ship.default: She bears me onward still, out of {home}, and long may the very heavens smile upon so fine a partnership.
ship.bounty: , a princely {bounty}g pledged to whatever wretch would dare unseat me

island.haven: The black flag usurps our banner now, and this once-proud chronicle keeps nothing but the sorry roll of the drowned and the damned.
island.default: {place} endures in splendour beneath our hand — {population} souls, and not the least of them but owes their quiet peace to us.

quiet.ship: Little of consequence graces these pages — a placid passage — and shall a man of my parts not permit the sea one small interval of calm?
quiet.island: Little disturbs our dominion this season; and is not a tranquil realm the surest monument that may be raised to the wisdom of its ruler?

phrases: , the {ord} such conquest to adorn my name
— as I have done, and shall assuredly do again
, another jewel set in my crown of victories
, the {ord} proud town I have humbled unto ashes
, the {ord} wolf I have hunted to his utter ruin
— another villain swept from the sea by this hand alone
— for what tempest of foes has ever yet unmade me?
